title: The Effectiveness of Slow-Release Fluoride Resin Modified Glass Ionomer Cement in the Treatment of Initial Active Proximal Caries Lesions A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial
summary: This study is investigating whether a new and simple application method of a dental material (RMGIC), which gradually releases fluoride, can effectively halt the progression of early proximal carious lesions in children when applied closely to the proximal area. This material will be compared with the standard treatments children typically receive to prevent caries. Also, it will be assessed whether the carious lesions progress over a year using x-ray and specialized dental images. Additionally,  factors such as the durability of the material and the health of the surrounding gums will be evaluated. The aim is to determine if this innovative method can provide better protection against further tooth decay in high caries risk children.

interventions.name:
Control group
-Education on dietary habits.
-Oral hygiene instruction, advice to use fluoride toothpaste (1450 ppm daily) and Elmex gel (12500 ppm) once a week at home.
 -Professional flossing and fluoride application with Clinpro™ White varnish (3M) with 5% sodium fluoride (22,600 ppm).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1)	Children with high risk of caries.
2)	Cooperative children. Only Code 3 and 4 according to Frankl behavior rating scale 
3)	Children willing to actively participate and appear to follow-up 
4)	The existence of the written declaration of consent of the study participants or their legal guardians.
- Inclusion criteria for tooth selection
1)	‎Primary molar or permanent molar or premolar with initial proximal caries lesions ‎extending radiographically to the enamel ‎(E1, E2), or the outer one third of dentine, just passing the EDJ (D1). (Young et al., 2015)
2)	Activity of the lesion: bleeding on probing in the proximal area of the lesion will be used as a criterion to assess the activity of the lesion.
Exclusion criteria:
1)	Children with general diseases and allergies.
2)	Patient with dry mouth.
3)	Patients who have already bitewings no older than 9 months but older than 1 month
4)	Children whose parents are not willing to participate in the study, and refuse to return back for follow-up visits and most importantly after 12 months for a second bitewing radiograph.
